# Exporting Log Data to Amazon S3

## Overview

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group named my-log-group to an Amazon S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets that are encrypted by AWS KMS is supported, but exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## Bucket requirements

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export; CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

## Permissions to create the export task

To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups. Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions, as documented in the access permissions section.

## Setting up bucket access permissions (same account)

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken, and it may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command then sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects.

If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

## SSE-KMS encryption (optional)

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. The KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt. The aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json creates the KMS key. The aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. If the put-bucket-encryption command doesn't return an error, the process is successful.

## Creating the export task

The create-export-task command creates the export task and returns a taskId. After you create an export task, it might take anywhere from a few seconds to a few hours, depending on the size of the data to export.

## Cross-account export

For cross-account export, you must first create a new IAM policy enabling CloudWatch Logs to have the s3:PutObject action for the destination bucket in the destination account. This policy has two conditional additions:

- If the destination bucket uses KMS encryption, the policy must add the kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt actions for the key resource.
- If ACLs are enabled on the destination bucket, the policy must add the s3:PutObjectAcl action.

To create an export task in the cross-account case, you must be signed in with an IAM role that has the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy attached, the IAM policy you created, and the logs permissions.

The cross-account bucket policy includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the exporting account to perform s3:PutObject with the s3:x-amz-acl condition bucket-owner-full-control. For cross-account SSE-KMS export, the KMS key policy must also allow the IAM role used for creating the export task to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

You can create an export task that exports all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group named `my-log-group` to an Amazon S3 bucket named `amzn-s3-demo-bucket`. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## Before you begin

Complete the prerequisites that apply to your case before creating the export task.

Same-account export:

- A CloudWatch Logs log group (`my-log-group`) to export, already created.
- A destination S3 bucket in the same Region as the log data (steps on this page).
- A bucket policy on the destination S3 bucket that allows the CloudWatch Logs regional service principal to export, with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` conditions (steps on this page).

- A destination S3 bucket in the destination account, in the same Region as the logs (steps on this page).
- An IAM identity policy granting CloudWatch Logs `s3:PutObject` on the destination bucket, plus `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt` if KMS is used, and `s3:PutObjectAcl` if ACLs are enabled (steps on this page).
- A signed-in IAM role with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess, the created policy, and the logs permissions (steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html).
- A bucket policy on the destination S3 bucket allowing CloudWatch Logs export, with source account conditions (steps on this page).

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure.

The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export. CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

# Exporting Log Data to Amazon S3 with CloudWatch Logs

## Overview

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group named my-log-group to an Amazon S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets encrypted by AWS KMS is supported, but exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## Bucket requirements

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export, because CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

## Access permissions

To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups. Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions as documented in this access permissions section.

## Setting the bucket policy (same-account export)

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains by default. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken, and it may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command then sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects.

If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

## SSE-KMS encryption (optional)

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. The KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt. The aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json creates the KMS key. The aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command then applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket, using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. If the put-bucket-encryption command doesn't return an error, the process is successful.

## Creating the export task

The create-export-task command creates the export task and returns a taskId. After you create an export task, it might take anywhere from a few seconds to a few hours to complete, depending on the size of the data to export.

The cross-account bucket policy includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the exporting account to perform s3:PutObject with the s3:x-amz-acl condition bucket-owner-full-control. For cross-account SSE-KMS export, the KMS key policy must also allow the IAM role used for creating the export task to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions, as documented in this access permissions section. To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups.

## Setting up the bucket policy (same-account export)

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains by default. The resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken, and it may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command then sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects. If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. In that case, the KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt. The aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json creates the KMS key. The aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command then applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket, using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. repair.regen_doc:
# Exporting log data to Amazon S3

An export task can export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group named my-log-group to an Amazon S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. Exporting log data to S3 buckets that are encrypted by AWS KMS is supported. Exporting to buckets encrypted with DSSE-KMS is not supported, so a bucket cannot be both a supported KMS export target and a DSSE-KMS bucket. The details of how you set up the export depend on whether the Amazon S3 bucket is in the same account as the logs being exported or in a different account.

## Before you begin

Same-account export:

- A CloudWatch Logs log group (my-log-group) containing the data to export.
- A destination S3 bucket in the same Region as the logs (steps on this page).
- A bucket policy on the destination S3 bucket allowing the CloudWatch Logs service principal to put objects and get the bucket ACL, with aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn conditions (steps on this page).
- Permissions for the signed-in identity: AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess plus logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups, granted through an IAM role, permission set, or user permissions (steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/howtocreatepermissionset.html).
- A KMS key policy allowing CloudWatch Logs to use the key, only if the destination bucket uses SSE-KMS (steps on this page).
- Bucket default encryption configured with the KMS key, only if exporting to an SSE-KMS bucket (steps on this page).

Cross-account export:

- A destination S3 bucket in the same Region as the logs, in the destination account (steps on this page).
- An IAM identity policy granting CloudWatch Logs s3:PutObject on the destination bucket, plus kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt if the bucket uses KMS, and s3:PutObjectAcl if ACLs are enabled, attached to the exporting role (steps on this page).
- An IAM role for the exporting user with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess, the policy above, and the logs export permissions (steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/howtocreatepermissionset.html).
- A bucket policy on the destination S3 bucket allowing CloudWatch Logs to export, with source accounts listed (steps on this page).

## Create the S3 bucket

AWS recommends using a bucket that was created specifically for CloudWatch Logs. If you want to use an existing bucket, you can skip the bucket creation procedure. The S3 bucket must reside in the same Region as the log data to export. CloudWatch Logs doesn't support exporting data to S3 buckets in a different Region.

## Set permissions on the bucket

To create the export task, you must be signed on with the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess IAM role and with the permissions logs:CreateExportTask, logs:CancelExportTask, logs:DescribeExportTasks, logs:DescribeLogStreams, and logs:DescribeLogGroups. Creating an export task requires signing in with sufficient permissions as documented in the access permissions section, and this must happen before you create the task.

By default, all S3 buckets and objects are private. Only the resource owner, the account that created the bucket, can access the bucket and any objects it contains by default. Because the bucket is private, the resource owner can grant access permissions to other resources and users by writing an access policy.

AWS now requires you to specify the list of source accounts that are allowed to export log data to your S3 bucket. The account IDs in the aws:SourceAccount key are the accounts from which a user can export log data to your S3 bucket. The aws:SourceArn key is the resource for which the action is being taken and may be restricted to a specific log group or use a wildcard. AWS recommends including the account ID of the account where the S3 bucket is created, to allow export within the same account.

Create the bucket policy file with a text editor, not the IAM console. The put-bucket-policy command then sets the access policy that enables CloudWatch Logs to export log data to your S3 bucket. This works only when the access policy has been written (the resource owner's ability to grant access) and the source accounts have been specified. The command must be run before you create the export task. The bucket owner will have full permissions on all of the exported objects.

If the existing bucket already has policies attached, you should add the CloudWatch Logs access statements to those policies. AWS recommends evaluating the resulting set of permissions to be sure they are appropriate for the users who will access the bucket.

## (Optional) SSE-KMS encryption

The SSE-KMS procedure is necessary only if you are exporting to an S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys, which is the case because KMS-encrypted export is supported. In that case the KMS key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal logs.Region.amazonaws.com to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

First, run the aws kms create-key command with key_policy.json to create the KMS key. Only after the key exists, run the aws s3api put-bucket-encryption command, which applies the bucketencryption.json configuration to the bucket using the aws:kms SSE algorithm with BucketKeyEnabled set to true. If the put-bucket-encryption command doesn't return an error, the process is successful.

## Cross-account export

For cross-account export, you must first create a new IAM policy enabling CloudWatch Logs to have the s3:PutObject action for the destination bucket in the destination account. If the destination bucket uses KMS encryption, the policy must add the kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt actions for the key resource. If ACLs are enabled on the destination bucket, the policy must add the s3:PutObjectAcl action.

To create an export task, you must be signed in with an IAM role that has the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy attached, the IAM policy you created, and the logs permissions.

The cross-account bucket policy includes a statement allowing an IAM role in the exporting account to perform s3:PutObject with the s3:x-amz-acl condition bucket-owner-full-control. For cross-account SSE-KMS export, the KMS key policy must also allow the IAM role used for creating the export task to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.

## Create the export task

The create-export-task command creates the export task and returns a taskId. In the cross-account case, the task can be created only when both the IAM policy described above has been created and the signed-in role has the required managed policy, the created policy, and the logs permissions. Before running it, the sign-in permissions and the bucket policy must be in place. After you create an export task, it might take anywhere from a few seconds to a few hours, depending on the size of the data to export.
